generic_inputs.value: Use the FINAL CURRENT requirements visible today as the normative baseline for evaluating every persisted nonce run. Do not require reconstruction of the original Agents.md/source/Step-3 revision merely to decide run compliance. Historical information is needed primarily to reconstruct CHANGES IN DESIRED REQUIREMENTS and instruction lineage: what the user wanted at each point, which requirements survived into the final requirements, which were superseded, and which were never implemented. A historical nonce may therefore be re-evaluated against today's final requirements even if those requirements did not exist when the run executed. Keep separate the question 'does this historical run satisfy the final current requirements?' from the instruction-lineage question 'what requirements changed over time, and which unsuperseded requirements were never implemented?'

evaluation_heuristic: DESIGN-ONLY. Revise the historical audit staging plan using audit_correction as authoritative. Treat current_agents_md, current_runtime_source, and current_step3_evaluation as the FINAL CURRENT requirement/implementation baseline against which every persisted Supervisor nonce run may be evaluated. Do not require historical contract snapshots as a prerequisite for nonce-run compliance. History is instead used to reconstruct the evolution of DESIRED REQUIREMENTS and user instruction lineage. Design two linked analyses: A) FINAL-BASELINE RUN AUDIT: evaluate each nonce run's persisted state/messages/store evidence against today's final requirements and implementation expectations, reporting which current requirements the run satisfies or fails; B) REQUIREMENT-LINEAGE AUDIT: reconstruct atomic user-requested requirements over time and classify each as IMPLEMENTED, SUPERSEDED_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION, MISSING_STILL_OUTSTANDING, or INDETERMINATE. A requirement that was later superseded is not a defect. A MISSING_STILL_OUTSTANDING requirement must be both never implemented and not later superseded, and still relevant under the final desired requirement set. Also define a requirements-delta artifact that tracks when desired requirements were added, modified, superseded, or retained into the final requirement set.
